Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NexCart Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing up for questions will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NexCart Inc.'s Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, COO; Morgan Patel, CMO; Riley Chen, CTO; Casey Lopez, CDO; and Jordan Ellis, CSO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of NexCart Inc.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by exceptional mobile app engagement that saw downloads surge and active users hit new highs, alongside navigating seasonality trends effectively despite some deviations from holiday peaks. We saw significant growth in key metrics like GMV up 22% year-over-year to $65 billion and active customers expanding 15% to 150 million.

Our focus remains on accelerating seller services and value-added services, where adoption rates are climbing and contributing meaningfully to revenue mix. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our new launches like ShopGenius AI personalization and NovaVital private label wellness line, which we believe will significantly boost conversion rates and customer loyalty.

We are investing heavily in enhancing seller performance, growing active sellers and revenue per seller through better tools and fulfillment.

We are focused on improving operating expense efficiency, leveraging automation to drive leverage against revenue growth.

We are expanding our presence amid macroeconomic factors, maintaining GMV momentum despite inflation and rate pressures.

We are enhancing our customer experience through AI-driven personalization and quick commerce pilots.

Finally, we are committed to lifting average order value through smarter bundling and premium category pushes.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q2 revenue was $15.0 billion, an increase of 25% year-over-year. Gross margin was 42%, driven by higher private label mix and fulfillment scale efficiencies. Operating expenses were $11.0 billion, representing 73% of revenue. Marketing spend rose 15% to $2.2 billion but as a percentage of revenue declined to 15%, thanks to performance marketing shifts and app-driven traffic lowering CAC to $28.

Our net income for the quarter was $1.2 billion, or $0.85 per share. We ended the quarter with $10 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of revenue $65-68 billion and adjusted EBITDA margins of 14-15%.

Let me expand on some key drivers behind these results, starting with our mobile app engagement, which continues to be a cornerstone as we lean into a mobile-first strategy where over 65% of e-commerce traffic comes from apps. In Q2, we hit 5.2 million new downloads globally, up 28% year-over-year from 4.1 million and 12% sequentially from Q1's 4.6 million, bringing cumulative downloads to 185 million. Catalysts included our summer flash sales using Apple Search Ads and Google campaigns at 4.2x ROAS, plus our referral program generating 1.8 million installs. North America led with 2.1 million, APAC surged 45% to 1.9 million via localized efforts outpacing competitors, Europe added 1 million, and emerging markets like Brazil and UAE showed early promise.

Monthly active users reached 18.7 million, up 32% YoY and 9% sequentially, with DAU at 4.9 million and a strong 26% DAU/MAU ratio above industry averages. Retention improved across Day 1, 7, and 30 metrics, powered by ML personalization navigating ATT challenges. Power users grew to 28% of MAU with double ARPU, sessions per DAU up to 4.2, and churn down to 4.2% monthly via predictive models.

Conversion rates climbed to 8.7%, up 21% YoY, outperforming web channels, with add-to-cart at 22% and abandonment at 28%. Category leaders like apparel at 11.2% benefited from live shopping, and APAC hit 10.1%. This drove app GMV to $2.8 billion, 58% of total and up 42% YoY, with superior margins from lower fraud and higher LTV. Underpinning this were app updates like faster loads, ML feeds, and Instagram integrations, with Q3 bringing NFTs and 5G features. We're targeting 25 million MAU by year-end.

Shifting to seasonality, our patterns remain predictable with Q4 peaks at 35-40% of annual GMV from holidays, Q1 troughs, Q2 ramps from summer events, and Q3 BTS bridges. Q2 GMV hit $3.1 billion up 18% YoY, slightly below 22% trend due to macro inflation hitting apparel, supply disruptions delaying inventory, Prime Day pull-forward, and weather. Positives included summer campaigns lifting beauty and Prime+ subscriptions flattening volatility. Regionally, APAC outperformed, North America and Europe lagged. Our AI forecasting at 92% accuracy, omnichannel BOPIS, and private labels are smoothing cycles, targeting Q3 $3.9-4.0 billion.

Seller services and value-added services revenue reached $3.52 billion, up 38% YoY, 23.5% of total revenue at 72% margins. Adoption hit 68% of 2.1 million sellers, with ads at 52% generating $2.1 billion, fulfillment at 41% $850 million, payments $360 million, and analytics $210 million. Multi-service sellers drove 65% revenue, ARS up 27% to $1,680. North America 52%, APAC exploding at 48% growth. Tech like Seller OS 2.0 and bots boost this, expecting 26% of revenue by FY25.

On new product launches, ShopGenius AI suite drove 35% conversion lift to 5.7%, $185 million incremental GMV, NPS 72. NovaVital wellness line hit $120 million GMV at 52% margins, 41% repeat rate. NovaNow quick commerce $45 million in first month, NPS 75. These contributed 12% to QoQ GMV growth, with strong regional traction and feedback guiding iterations.

Seller performance metrics show 1.2 million actives up 18% YoY, revenue per seller $1,450 up 12%, GMV per seller $28,500. North America 620k, APAC 380k surging. Onboarding cut to 18 days, SFN adoption 42% lifting GMV 35%, targeting 20% growth.

Operating expenses efficiency shone with total OpEx up 12% YoY to 74% of revenue, improving 320bps. Fulfillment down to 9.4% of GMV via MFCs and robots, marketing CAC down 19%, tech R&D yielding quick ROI, G&A flat headcount. Private labels and EV fleets aid leverage, guiding 72-74% for FY24.

Macro factors tempered growth with inflation, rates, and disruptions shaving 400bps off GMV, hitting discretionary categories and logistics up 12%. Trade-down to essentials, but ads up 22%, private labels buffered. Counters include GenAI pricing, EV fleets, regional plays, guiding Q4 resilient.

Finally, AOV rose 8.2% YoY to $85.20 via premium mix up 5.6%, AI upsells 3.2%, shipping thresholds. Headwinds like promo intensity mitigated, targeting 7-9% H2 growth with BOPIS and subscriptions.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor Kim to discuss operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on supply chain resilience and fulfillment optimization. Our shipping times improved by 25%. Fulfillment costs were down 15%. We are implementing robotic automation in 80% of centers.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan Patel.

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from summer flash sales and TikTok live events. Customer acquisition costs were $28. Our brand awareness increased by 20%. We are focusing on app ASO and performance channels.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Chen.

Riley Chen:
Thanks, Morgan. On the technology front, we've been focused on edge caching and ML recommendations. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 32%. We're investing in GenAI for voice commerce.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey Lopez.

Casey Lopez:
Thanks, Riley. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 21% improvement in conversion rates because of personalization models. We are also focusing on privacy-compliant server-side tracking.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan Ellis.

Jordan Ellis:
Thanks, Casey. Sustainability is very important to us. We reduced our carbon footprint by 25%. We are committed to 100% recycled packaging and EV fleet expansion.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will be conducting a question-and-answer session. [Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Thanks. On mobile app engagement, can you elaborate on regional drivers and future tech like NFTs?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, John. As Jordan detailed, APAC's 45% download growth came from hyper-local campaigns and UPI, while North America's BNPL integrations helped. Retention gains from ML onboarding are key. Q3 NFTs for loyalty will target high-LTV users, building on our 1.7x app conversion uplift.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
Regarding seasonality deviations in Q2, what mitigated the macro and supply issues?

Jordan Lee:
Emily, inflation accounted for 40% of the 4-point miss, supply chain 30%. Our AI forecasting reclaimed 3% GMV via dynamic pricing, Prime+ flattened volatility by 8%, and APAC's 28% growth offset North America softness. Q3 BTS looks strong.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

David Rodriguez:
Seller services adoption is impressive—how are you driving multi-VAS uptake?

Taylor Kim:
David, seamless API onboarding and incentives for $50K GMV thresholds got us to 68% adoption. Multi-VAS sellers at 420k contribute 65% revenue, with Seller OS 2.0's predictive tools reducing stockouts 35%. APAC fulfillment at 45% is a highlight.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wang with Barclays.

Lisa Wang:
Early feedback on new launches like NovaNow—any scaling plans?

Morgan Patel:
Lisa, NPS 75 on NovaNow reflects speed appeal, with 62% retention. We're addressing perishables stockouts via Nielsen-integrated forecasting, expanding MFCs to 50 by year-end. ShopGenius' 35% CVR lift and NovaVital's 4x target beat show personalization and private labels working.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Thompson with Citi.

Mike Thompson:
Seller metrics growth is solid—thoughts on ARPAS sustainability?

Riley Chen:
Mike, 12% ARPAS rise to $1,450 from ads ROAS 4.2x and SFN's 22% uplift. Seller 360 tier already at 120k subs boosting 40%, with APAC cross-border tools driving $1,800 there. $150M capex for centers supports 15% expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Kim with Deutsche Bank.

Anna Kim:
OpEx leverage details—fulfillment efficiencies?

Casey Lopez:
Anna, 180bps drop to 9.4% of GMV from Nexus MFCs cutting pick times 35%, AMRs coming to 80% facilities. Marketing ROAS 8.2x, tech cloud savings 28%. Fixed-variable mix flexes with demand.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Hayes with RBC Capital.

Robert Hayes:
Macro impact and AOV—how are you countering trade-down?

Jordan Ellis:
Robert, macros shaved 400bps GMV, but private labels like NexVital grew 35% at 45% margins. AOV up 8.2% from bundles and SmartCart upsells at 42% attach. EV fleets cut costs 18%, regional localization like India voice search aids resilience.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
